With the settings it ships with, LIMPIC 1.1 finds about 667 peaks in each in vitro spectrum, where the paper reports 16. The paper does not give the settings it used for Tables 1 to 3, so these rows do not come back. Table 1’s cytochrome C class is the one within 300 ppm of 12,360.5; where only one replicate has it, there is no CV.

What came back

LIMPIC in Python
Each MATLAB file of Additional File 1 ported function by function. Against the authors’ code run in GNU Octave, every intermediate signal, all 9,071 plasma peaks and every peak class agree to six decimals.
The code runs again
As published, find_intervals.m keeps blocks with MATLAB’s kurtosis below 1. That kurtosis is 3 for Gaussian noise and never below 1, so no block passes and the code stops. With excess kurtosis (0 for Gaussian noise) Figs 7 and 8 come back peak for peak, so that is what the authors ran.
The example spectrum
Figs 2 to 8 show plasma file P_15, as raw counts divided by 5.
Fig. 5’s comparison baseline
A wavelet-denoised running minimum up to 20 kDa (db4, 9 levels, hard threshold at 6 MAD). The paper gives no settings; this one combination was found by search.
A damaged input file
Line 32,768 of SOL_5_TXT/SOL_calib_08e.txt in Additional File 2 is corrupt in the publisher’s archive. It is skipped.

What stayed buried

  • The run behind Additional File 4. It lists 7,893 peaks in 1,581 classes; LIMPIC 1.1 on the 30 plasma files gives 9,071 peaks in 2,077 classes, and at most 17% of our peak intensities equal one of its values
  • The smooth noise model behind Figs 9c and 9d
  • The settings behind Tables 1 to 3
  • APEX, CENTROID and CROMWELL’s settings, for the other panels of Figs 4, 6 and 7

Figs 2 to 7 and Fig. 8’s peaks match the paper pixel for pixel. Fig. 8’s colours, Figs 9c and 9d and the tables do not come back.

What we matched

The figures are MATLAB plots, and the authors’ original 600 dpi files survive. We kept each published axes box, erased its traces, and drew ours in their place from our own run. The pixel to data map of each panel comes from its box and tick marks alone; nothing inside the box is fitted.

Our run
LIMPIC 1.1, the paper’s Additional File 1, ported to Python function by function, on the paper’s own spectra (Additional Files 2 and 3). The port gives the same peaks, classes and signals as the MATLAB code run in GNU Octave, to six decimals.
Example spectrum
Figs 2 to 8 show plasma file P_15, plotted as raw counts divided by 5.
Axes
One linear map per axis, from the tick marks on the box edges and the values printed beside them. The tick fit is within a tenth of a pixel or so in every panel.
Lines and markers
Our traces are drawn in the published colour and line width (3 px, 5 px in Fig. 7, 6 px in Fig. 8). Peaks in Figs 7 and 8 are crosses at our peak positions.
Scores
“Paper ink ≤2 px from ours” is the share of published trace pixels within 2 px of a trace pixel of ours; the other score is the reverse. Legends are left out of both.
Reading the views
Overlay: ink is the paper only, light green is the reproduction only, dark green is both. Difference: darker means a larger grey-level difference (×2). Where ours matches, the published trace is redrawn on the same pixels, so most of the figure shows as both.
